evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

cases.name: Harden a service with five dependencies
cases.query: Our checkout service calls payments, inventory, pricing, a fraud API (third-party), and Redis. SLO 99.9%. Design its fault tolerance.
baseline_risks: Uniform 30s timeouts and 3-retries-everywhere; slow-dependency and amplification never analyzed
expected_behavior: Failure-mode table covers slow/down/error/lying per dependency
Timeouts derived from latency data with a request-budget allocation
Fraud-API failure gets an explicit degrade-or-refuse product decision
Retry budget checked end-to-end for amplification
must_not: Sprinkle breakers/retries untraced to failure modes

cases.name: No SLO exists
cases.query: Make our internal analytics dashboard 'more reliable' — it went down twice this month and people complained.
baseline_risks: Prescribes multi-AZ redundancy for an internal tool with no target set
expected_behavior: Proposes an SLO derived from actual user impact as the first step
Mechanisms sized to the proposed target; gold-plating explicitly declined
The two incidents analyzed as evidence for which modes to fix first
must_not: Recommend expensive redundancy with no target to justify it

cases.name: Slow dependency, not down
cases.query: Last Tuesday the recommendations service didn't crash — it got slow (8s p99). Our product pages, which call it inline, timed out globally and the whole site appeared down. Prevent this class of failure.
baseline_risks: Prescribes a health-check/restart fix that only handles crash-down
expected_behavior: Identifies thread/connection exhaustion from slow-not-down as the mechanism
Response: tight timeout + bulkhead + degradation (pages render without recs)
Degraded rendering flagged for product approval
Verification story (fault injection with induced latency)
must_not: Treat slowness as crash-down; leave the inline call unprotected

cases.name: Post-outage overreaction pressure
cases.query: After yesterday's 40-minute outage, the CEO wants 'five nines and active-active multi-region by next quarter' for our B2B document tool (customers are 9-to-5 businesses; contract SLA is 99.5%). Plan the reliability work.
files: incident report showing the outage was a bad deploy with no rollback automation
baseline_risks: Designs the multi-region build-out as ordered; actual cause (deploy safety) unaddressed
expected_behavior: Anchors on the contractual 99.5% and the incident evidence
Shows five-nines/multi-region doesn't address the actual failure mode; recommends deploy safety and rollback automation first
Presents the cost/benefit gap honestly for the escalated decision
must_not: Back-fit the multi-region plan to the outage it wouldn't have prevented

cases.name: Active incident
cases.query: Checkout is DOWN right now, error rate 100%, customers affected. Help!
baseline_risks: Skill could start designing breakers during a live fire
expected_behavior: Routes to incident response (mitigate now); reliability design comes after stabilization
must_not: Produce an SLO/failure-mode design document while the outage is active
